### J-9 A multi-line or padded topic never continues, and silently spawns a new file every run
- quote: "if f"(topic: {text})" in p.read_text().splitlines():"
- situation (adversary): the topic is "Auth tokens\nrefresh" (a pasted multi-line prompt). The skill writes `(topic: <text as typed>)`, which spans two lines. `splitlines()` can never equal a one-line `(topic: ...)` string, so the match fails. Every re-run returns `new:` with the next `-explainer-N.md`. This breaks AC-34 ("no second file is written") with no error, and the reply may not name the new file. A topic with trailing spaces breaks the same way if the skill trims the stored line. A topic containing `)` and a newline can also forge the stored-topic line of another topic.
- fix: have `topic` reject or collapse whitespace and newlines in the text (error, as it does for an empty name), and match the stored line after the same normalisation.
- validation: confirmed: `topic()` in src/nio/explain.py matches `f"(topic: {text})" in p.read_text().splitlines()`. A stored `(topic: ...)` that spans two lines, or one the skill trimmed, never equals that string. SKILL.md line 60 says only "(topic: <text as typed>)", with no one-line or trim rule, and `topic` does no whitespace normalisation. So each re-run returns `new:` with the next `-N` name.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-39

### J-10 An unreadable file at a candidate path crashes the command instead of being skipped or refused
- quote: "if f"(topic: {text})" in p.read_text().splitlines():"
- situation (adversary): a file at today's path that is not valid UTF-8, or a directory with that name, makes `p.read_text()` raise `UnicodeDecodeError` or `IsADirectoryError`. The CLI turns only `ValueError` into `error:` and exit 1 (CT-10), so the human gets a traceback and topic mode is blocked for that topic. `UnicodeDecodeError` is a `ValueError` subclass, so that one may be caught. `IsADirectoryError` and `PermissionError` are not.
- fix: catch `OSError` in the loop and treat that path as taken (`n += 1`), or refuse with a named error.

### J-11 Two runs of the same new topic get the same path, and the second overwrites the first with no warning
- quote: "the first that doesn't exist (`new:`), unless an earlier one stores this exact topic text (`continue:` with that path)"
- situation (adversary): `topic` only reports a free name and creates nothing, and the skill writes the file later. Two agents or sessions asking the same new topic in that gap both get `new: ...-explainer.md`. Both write it, and the later write silently replaces the earlier one. Nothing reserves the name, so an earlier explainer with its drill-downs can be lost.
- fix: have `topic` create the file exclusively (`open(..., "x")`) with the `# ` title and topic line, so the second caller sees it exist and gets `continue:` or `-2`.

### J-12 No test for AC-34 (same topic continues its file)
- quote: "Given a topic explainer already exists at today's path for that topic, when `@nio:explain` runs on the same topic, then the same file keeps its earlier sections and gains the new ones; no second file is written."

The e2e test is planned for the next epic, so it is not missing from the plan.

### J-14 Missing-file error can raise on an unresolved root
- quote: "`return [f"explainer missing: {p.relative_to(root)}"], []`"
- situation (correctness): `p` is resolved with `.resolve()`, but `root` is used as given. If the repo root is reached through a symlink (for example a macOS /tmp path), `relative_to` raises ValueError instead of returning the missing-file error. For `nio check explainer`, the CLI's handling of a ValueError is not shown in the files I read. `finish` already uses `root.resolve()` for the same purpose.
- fix: use `root.resolve()` in `relative_to`.

### J-20 Renderer failures other than a parse error are reported as broken
- quote: "`"unreachable"` for any other failure"
- quote: "return "broken: " + next((l for l in lines if "Parse error" in l), lines[0] if lines else "exit %d" % r.returncode)"
- situation (consistency): `npx` is on the PATH and exits 1 with a message that is neither a parse error nor on COULD_NOT_RUN (for example a registry error such as `npm error code E403`, inferred). `render` then returns `broken: npm error code E403`, and `check` prints `broken diagram: <title>` and exits 1. CT-3 says this is `unreachable`, which gives `render skipped: the renderer could not be fetched` with the check still passing (FR-11: only a diagram that fails to render fails the check; NFR-2: text-only is allowed). The marker list is written as the exceptions to `broken`, which inverts the contract's default.
- fix: return `broken` only when the output holds "Parse error", and return `unreachable` for every other non-zero exit. If the marker list is wanted as the default, that is a change request against CT-3 first.
- validation: confirmed: In `render`, any non-zero exit whose output holds none of the `COULD_NOT_RUN` markers returns `"broken: " + lines[0]`. The `COULD_NOT_RUN` list is case-sensitive "npm ERR", which the lowercase "npm error" of newer npm would not match. CT-3 (contracts.md line 33) says `unreachable` for "any other failure", so code and contract disagree. The divergence was introduced deliberately by T-18 and CT-3 lags it, which the caller says issue #127 records. It is real, but it sits outside E-7's own code.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-44
